## Upstream changes 19.5.6 -> 19.6.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no release notes could be read for this range, so nothing in GitLab EE 19.6.0 can be confirmed safe; the registry image configurations also could not be read (404), so no verdict-level mismatch could be checked there either. Treat this as an unverified jump and check by hand before applying.

### Breaking changes
- none found in the notes — the notes source returned nothing: "(not available: no releases between 19.5.6 and 19.6.0 found under gitlabhq/gitlabhq (0 releases read), and no tag range compared)". This is an absence of data, not a confirmation of no breaking changes.

### Variables
- none found in the notes. The compose file and .env.example are unchanged in content supplied; no renamed/removed/newly-required variables are evidenced for this range.

### Data and dependencies
- Already true at the current version (19.5.6), not introduced by this range: the compose file pins `postgres:17` and the `postgres` command sets `max_locks_per_transaction=256`, with the comment noting "GitLab's schema load and migrations exhaust PostgreSQL's default lock table ... GitLab's external-database guidance calls for a raised max_locks_per_transaction." This is a pre-existing requirement, not a change from this upgrade.
- Whether GitLab 19.6.0 raises its minimum/recommended PostgreSQL version beyond 17, or changes any other companion-service requirement, is unknown — the notes that would state this could not be read.

### Before applying
- Take a full GitLab backup (`gitlab-backup.sh` per this repo's README) and a Postgres volume/data snapshot before touching the running stack — standard precaution given no migration notes are available to rule out irreversible schema changes.
- Manually check the official GitLab 19.6.0 release post and the GitLab Omnibus/Docker upgrade documentation (gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab releases and the UPGRADING notes) for:
  - any required intermediate upgrade stops between 19.5.6 and 19.6.0 (GitLab enforces these periodically),
  - PostgreSQL minimum-version changes,
  - background-migration or Sidekiq requirements that must finish before/after upgrading,
  - Gitaly/Workhorse or other bundled-component changes affecting the single `gitlab-ee` image.
- Re-check the registry for the actual image digest/config of `gitlab/gitlab-ee:19.6.0-ee.0` once reachable, and diff user/entrypoint/command/ports/volumes/healthcheck/environment against 19.5.6-ee.0 before trusting this report's silence on that point.

### Notes read
- None. GitLabHQ release notes for the 19.5.6 → 19.6.0 range could not be found (0 releases read, no tag range compared). Image registry metadata for both tags also could not be read (HTTP 404). This review is based solely on the compose file and .env.example as supplied.

## Upstream changes v3.8.10 -> v3.8.11

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no companion-service version mismatch and no image-level config drift, but this release introduces irreversible, one-way database format upgrades that a multi-device setup can get wrong.

### Breaking changes
- Database format upgrades are one-way and version-gated. Per the notes: "Simply opening a database does not trigger these upgrades. Version 3.8.10 supports database formats up to 14. A client can only open databases in formats it supports. Update every device that syncs or accesses the same data before using the new formats. Back up your workspace beforehand. To roll back, restore a complete pre-upgrade snapshot." Two new formats are introduced: format 16 ("Saving new block rich text in a primary key, including text with images, upgrades the database to at least format 16") and format 17 ("Saving the first inline image in an ordinary text field upgrades that database to format 17"). If this host syncs its workspace with any other SiYuan device/client still on 3.8.10 or earlier, that device will be unable to open the workspace once these new rich-text or inline-image features are used here.
- Kernel API request size is now capped: "JSON requests handled by API contracts have a 32 MiB body limit, with a 64 KiB limit for `loginAuth`. Requests exceeding these limits return code `-1`." Any external script, plugin, or integration calling the kernel API with larger payloads will start failing with error code `-1`.
- AI long-term memory snapshot restore behaviour changed: "Restoring a workspace snapshot now rolls back both memory records and their revocation state. Restoring a snapshot from before a memory was forgotten can make it available again if it still passes the usual validity checks." Relevant only if the long-term memory feature (added in v3.8.10) is in use and snapshots are restored.

### Variables
none

### Data and dependencies
- none beyond the format-upgrade behaviour above — there is no separate database engine (SiYuan uses embedded SQLite via the image itself), so there is no companion-service version to check against the compose file.
- Already true at the current version (not introduced by this upgrade): the `command: ['serve', ...]` subcommand-CLI invocation and `SIYUAN_ACCESS_AUTH_CODE` environment variable, as noted in the compose file's own comment — this template already runs that way at v3.8.10.

### Before applying
- Back up the workspace before upgrading, as the notes explicitly instruct: "Back up your workspace beforehand." The compose file's `backups` service already does this continuously, but confirm a recent successful backup exists (check the container logs for a `Data backup OK` line) before pulling the new image.
- If this workspace is synced to or opened by any other SiYuan installation (desktop, mobile, another server), upgrade all of them to v3.8.11 before any of them create new primary-key rich text with images or inline images in ordinary text fields — otherwise those other clients will be locked out of the workspace once the format is upgraded.
- No .env or compose edits needed; bump `SIYUAN_IMAGE_VERSION` (or the `x-images` pin) to `v3.8.11` and redeploy.
